articles.title: This Is Why I Love Wrestling
articles.description: Sometimes in wrestling, you only need one good day. Chael Sonnen tells the story of Blaine Natal, a wrestler he's known and coached for years. Blaine has spent his life showing up, taking the hard matches and refusing to let failure determine whether he steps on the mat again. His mother, Candy, has been there for all of it. But for all the years of work, Blaine was still waiting for that day. Then he drew Noah Wachsmuth, an undefeated Oregon champion and former Olympic Training Center athlete. On paper, this wasn't supposed to be Blaine's moment. For much of the match, it didn't look like it would be. But wrestling doesn't reward how impressive something looks. The scoreboard does the talking. When time expired, Blaine had one more point. After 22 years, he finally had his day. For Chael, it was one of those rare moments in sports that brought a tear to his eye. You don't need 10 years of perfect days. Sometimes you just need one.
